writing.title: Large Data Volumes Are Not Your Performance Problem
writing.ai_summary: Agent-driven analytics workloads, not data volume, are the real performance problem; sampling and heavy aggregation strip the fine-grained signals multi-step reasoning needs. Separating compute from storage lets query execution, ingestion, and background tasks scale independently.

writing.title: Ten years of open source: a stained-glass view
writing.ai_summary: ClickHouse marks ten years of open source with a stained-glass analogy, covering 2,632 contributors queryable in system.contributors, 99% of pull requests closed, the Champions recognition program, and Memorial Sloan Kettering's cBioPortal running cancer queries about ten times faster.

writing.title: Agentic AI – The Cambrian Moment for Data Architectures
writing.ai_summary: Agentic AI workloads break data architectures built for batch reports and human-paced analysis. Tyler Hannan of ClickHouse covers concurrency cliffs, why sampling means amnesia for agents, and a readiness test measuring p95 latency and cost per workflow.

writing.title: ClickHouse at FOSDEM 2026
writing.ai_summary: ClickHouse's FOSDEM 2026 weekend in Brussels featured a 106-person community dinner and talks by Alexey Milovidov, Pablo Marcos, and Elmi Ahmadov on XRay hot-patching, inverted indexes, C++ and Rust integration, memcpy optimization, and real-time visualizations.

writing.title: ClickHouse at FOSDEM 2025: talks, tech, and a community dinner
writing.ai_summary: ClickHouse recaps its FOSDEM 2025 showing in Brussels, with talks by Robert Schulze on the new JSON data type, Pedro Ferreira on fuzzing databases with BuzzHouse, and Alexey Milovidov on an rDNS map, plus a community dinner.

writing.title: ClickHouse + Deepnote: Data Notebooks & Collaborative Analytics
writing.ai_summary: ClickHouse's new Deepnote integration lets teams query ClickHouse from Jupyter-compatible, cloud-based notebooks with first-class SQL support, no Python connector needed. A template project connects to the ClickHouse Playground, with a challenge to explore GitHub Archive data for a t-shirt.

writing.title: Case Study: Industrial IoT Platform Machine Metrics Increased Developer Velocity by 10x Using Hasura
writing.ai_summary: Industrial IoT platform MachineMetrics used Hasura with TimescaleDB to auto-generate GraphQL APIs over its machine data, boosting developer velocity 10x, enabling incremental migration from REST, and giving customers secure direct data access.

writing.title: Announcing The Hasura Contributor Program
writing.ai_summary: Hasura's new Contributor Program recognizes community work like code contributions, tutorials, translations, and answering questions on Discord and GitHub Discussions, with standout contributors earning the 'Hasura Champion' title. Roadmap ideas include event sponsorship, content support, and a Champions gallery.

writing.title: HasuraCon'21 - Cross Database Joins with GraphQL and all the other exciting announcements
writing.ai_summary: HasuraCon'21 announcements include the stable Hasura 2.0 release with multi-database support, REST endpoints and authorization upgrades, cross database joins with GraphQL, schema sharing, Git-based CI/CD on Hasura Cloud, and 250 million GraphQL Engine downloads.

writing.title: HasuraCon'21: Announcing the Hasura User Conference
writing.ai_summary: HasuraCon'21, a free two-day user conference, runs June 23-24 with speakers including Tanmai Gopal, Davy Stevenson, Guillermo Rauch of Vercel and Erik Reyna of the Washington Post. The CFP is open, covering Hasura production use-cases, modernisation stories and integrations.

writing.title: GraphQL and Government Technology
writing.ai_summary: GraphQL works in government and highly regulated environments, as Bharat Kashyap's GraphQL Asia talk on Samagra's education tech in Indian states shows. Topics include legacy migration, e-Samwad, scalability across a 200M-person region, and Hasura Cloud's SOC2 and HIPAA compliance.

writing.title: 10 months, 11 engineers, 3000 customers & $1B in tradable ARR - How Pipe is using Hasura
writing.ai_summary: Fintech startup Pipe, with 3000 customers and $1B in tradable ARR, went from Hasura discovery to production in 11 days with 11 engineers, cutting front-end developer needs by 50% and solving the n+1 problem out of the box.

writing.title: TimescaleDB 2.0 with Hasura Part 3 - High Availability
writing.ai_summary: High availability for TimescaleDB 2.0 with Hasura, covering single-node streaming replication with Patroni or repmgr, multi-node failures where only INSERT survives, and native replication's slower writes, with streaming replication recommended as the best multi-node option.

writing.title: TimescaleDB 2.0 with Hasura Part 2 - Multi-Node
writing.ai_summary: TimescaleDB 2.0 multi-node setup with Hasura: distributed hypertables insert 1 million rows in about 11 seconds, but UPDATE and DELETE run far slower than single-node, foreign keys fail so Hasura relationships need manual setup, and continuous aggregates aren't supported.

writing.title: Introducing - Hasura Advanced Tutorial
writing.ai_summary: Hasura launches its Advanced Tutorial, aimed at users optimizing applications for production, with newcomers pointed to Hasura Basics first. The MIT-licensed course lives on GitHub and will be live-streamed on Twitch and YouTube during #GraphQLJanuary.

writing.title: The New Data Fabric - Enterprise GraphQL
writing.ai_summary: James Governor's RedMonk talk "The New Data Fabric" from Hasura's October 2020 Enterprise GraphQL Conference, revisited during GraphQL January, covers the shift to two-tier apps, platform teams curating services, and GraphQL's separation of concerns between API builders and consumers.

writing.title: TimescaleDB 2.0 with Hasura
writing.ai_summary: TimescaleDB 2.0 with Hasura brings breaking changes from 1.7, including renamed policy functions and refactored continuous aggregates, plus GraphQL limits on hypertables without primary keys and a migration CLI workaround for transaction-block errors.

writing.title: 2020 Year In Review
writing.ai_summary: Hasura's 2020 recap walks month by month through v1.0.0 and v1.3.0 releases, Actions, Scheduled Triggers, Remote Joins, the Hasura Cloud launch, Series A and $25M Series B funding, and SOC2 Type 1 and HIPAA compliance.

writing.title: GraphQL Contributor Days - #GraphQLJanuary
writing.ai_summary: GraphQL Contributor Days, a nearly four-hour discussion among about 20 contributors, covers @defer and @stream directives, custom scalars, federated GraphQL execution, and error handling, launching Hasura's #GraphQLJanuary with weekly Discord Q&As.

writing.title: GraphQL January
writing.ai_summary: Hasura's GraphQL January event, starting 11 January 2021, helps developers learn GraphQL through daily blog posts, weekly language-specific Twitch livestreams building a full stack app, 30-minute tutorial videos, Discord Q&As, and Office Hours Zoom chats.

writing.title: Community Tooling at Hasura
writing.ai_summary: Hasura moved technical support to GitHub Discussions for searchability and the ability to turn discussions into tracked issues. Discord remains the community hub for chat and collaboration, alongside a monthly newsletter, community call, and office hours.

writing.title: Software Naming & Releases
writing.ai_summary: Fauna explains its software naming and release practices, covering monthly release cadence, Semantic Versioning for MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH versions, and what General Availability, Preview, Experimental and End-of-Life mean, including 12 months of support for each major release.

writing.title: Beta Release of Elastic Cloud on Google Cloud Platform (GCP), More Options to Host Elasticsearch
writing.ai_summary: Elastic Cloud's beta on Google Cloud Platform adds hosted Elasticsearch and Kibana alongside the existing AWS option, managed from the same console. Beta includes X-Pack features but only monthly standard subscriptions, no SLA, with GA planned for late 2017.

writing.title: Hosted Elasticsearch Services Roundup: Elastic Cloud and Amazon Elasticsearch Service
writing.ai_summary: A comparison of Elastic's Elasticsearch Service on Elastic Cloud and Amazon Elasticsearch Service, which Elastic doesn't build or support. Elastic Cloud runs on AWS, GCP, and Azure, includes X-Pack, offers same-day releases, and costs about 20% less in apples-to-apples comparisons.

writing.title: Riak and Mesos – Automating Scale
writing.ai_summary: Riak's alpha framework runs Riak KV on Apache Mesos and Mesosphere DCOS, letting users create clusters, add nodes, and view status via Riak Explorer; the scheduler spreads nodes across agents for fault tolerance, with a Zookeeper-based proxy tracking cluster changes.

writing.title: Relational to Riak Webinar – Highlights and Additional Resources
writing.ai_summary: Highlights from the "From Relational to Riak" webinar on why companies move off RDBMS, covering Riak's masterless high availability, consistent hashing for scalability, and flexible Key/Value data model, with a PostgreSQL posts database migration example.

writing.title: Gaming and Betting Companies Find Success with Riak
writing.ai_summary: Gaming and betting companies like bet365 and Riot Games use Riak for player data, session storage, and global data locality, replacing SQL and MySQL databases to handle massive scale, including League of Legends chat for 70 million players.

writing.title: Fundamentals of NoSQL Security
writing.ai_summary: NoSQL databases like Riak are no more or less secure than relational databases; Riak 2.0 adds authentication and authorization modeled on PostgreSQL, with trust, password, PAM, and certificate sources, and can meet HIPAA and PCI compliance.

writing.title: The Requirement of High Availability
writing.ai_summary: Riak argues high availability is an architectural decision, not a bolt-on feature, covering downtime costs, the "number of 9s" metric, its masterless Erlang design with hinted handoff, and Temetra's choice of Riak over Cassandra and Hadoop.

writing.title: Solving the Problem of Unstructured Data Using Distributed Systems
writing.ai_summary: Unstructured data growth from IoT and connected devices, a 2015 growth trend highlighted at CES, is the focus of an on-demand webinar by Dorothy Pults and Tyler Hannan on distributed databases like Riak, horizontal scale, and multi-datacenter replication.

writing.title: Data Modeling with Riak
writing.ai_summary: Data modeling in Riak's key/value store, covering query options like Riak Search with Apache Solr, Secondary Indexes and MapReduce, user and session data examples, conflict resolution via vector clocks and Active Anti-Entropy, and multi-datacenter replication in Riak Enterprise.

writing.title: Using Riak as a Document Store
writing.ai_summary: Riak 2.0 can serve as a document store for JSON data by combining the maps data type with Riak Search indexing, offering scalable, available storage with full-text queries, automatic conflict resolution, and multi-datacenter replication via Riak Enterprise.

writing.title: Values, Keys, Buckets, Bucket Types – Riak 2.0
writing.ai_summary: Riak 2.0 adds bucket types, a namespace above buckets and keys that lets groups of buckets share one configuration, managed operationally via riak-admin instead of client requests, so the same bucket name can hold different data.

writing.title: Replication is the Key for Scalability & High Availability
writing.ai_summary: Riak's automatic intra-cluster replication, with a default n_val of 3 keeping three copies on separate vnodes, provides high availability and fault tolerance. Riak Enterprise adds masterless multi-datacenter replication for data locality, disaster recovery, and global availability.

writing.title: Write it like Riak; Query it Like Solr
writing.ai_summary: Riak 2.0's Riak Search (Yokozuna) pairs Riak's distributed key-value store with Apache Solr full-text search, running a Solr instance on each node, supporting ad-hoc range and wildcard queries, and using Active Anti-Entropy to keep indexes fresh.

writing.title: Riak 2.0 – New Capabilities, New Use Cases, Available for Download
writing.ai_summary: Riak 2.0, in both open source and Riak Enterprise versions, adds distributed Solr search, built-in security with authentication and authorization, per-bucket strong consistency, and new Data Types like sets and maps, plus simplified configuration, bucket types, and tiered storage.
